title: runtime quick capture - omar
content:
Quick capture (morning + afternoon) - do not treat as polished

Date: 2026-03-12 / updated 2026-03-13
Owner: Omar Patel (serving-runtime)
Context: working-through a set of regressions after the attention-kernel swap + quiet KV-cache thrashing on prod-dedicated pools. Jotted notes, commands to reproduce, and immediate next steps.

Top priority items (today)
- P0: RINF-2123 - p50 regression on small-context chat paths (seq_len 64) after kernel-rewrite. Repro locally on dev-box with small_model_v2-quant.
- P1: KV-cache eviction spikes on certain traffic shapes (mostly multi-turn chat with many short requests). Intermittent.
- P1: Strange CUDA memgrowth observed on node-a-07 when doing mixed-batch throughput tests.

Repro notes / quick commands
- Repro p50 regression: 
  - git checkout fix/attention-simd-slow 
  - docker run --rm -e MODEL=small_model_v2-quant redwood/runtime:dev bash -c "./bench/throughput --seq 64 --batch 8 --warm 50 --iter 200"
  - local p50 observed: 45ms (expected baseline ~28ms)
  - profile: ./tools/profile.sh --target-pid $(pgrep runtime) --duration 15s  (look for L1/L2 miss increases around matmul kernel)

- KV-cache eviction repro:
  - script: scripts/kv/qps-burst.sh --profile chat-multi-turn --users 400 --burst 20 --turns 6 
  - watch /metrics cache_hit_rate, cache_evictions_total (prom endpoint: http://localhost:9090/metrics)
  - observed pattern: 20s after burst start, eviction rate spikes and p95 latency climbs x2

Quick triage notes (what I tried)
- Reverted the attention microkernel (~PR 987) locally: p50 drops back to 30-32ms (still 10% worse than stable, but much better than 45ms). Suggests both microkernel and scheduler change contributed.
- Disabled aggressive prefetch in runtime: small improvement (p50 -3ms).
- KV-cache: found bug in cache key equality when request has tool-call metadata header; duplicate entries created -> more memory and thrash. Patch idea: normalize headers when building prefix key.

Observations / hypotheses
- Kernel rewrite introduced a slightly different memory access pattern causing L2 thrash in some GPUs (Ampere). On T4 it's less visible. Suspect 2D tiling or loop-order sensitivity.
- Scheduler batching heuristics: after kernel change, batch packing produces slightly larger variance in request execution time -> reduces effective batching and raises queuing tail latencies.
- KV-cache metadata bug explains a subset of eviction spikes (mostly traffic with tool-calls + short context).

Immediate next actions (assignments)
- Omar: instrument kernel-level counters for L1/L2 miss rates in the perf wrapper, land small probe (RINF-2206) by EOD.
- Leila: take the cache-key normalizer patch and run long-term soak on preprod (ticket RINF-2211).
- Chen: run the gpu-tiling microbench suite on node-a-07 / node-a-09 (Ampere vs Ampere-2); capture nvprof output and upload to PR 987 thread.
- Sync: 11:30 standup quick sync in #eng-runtime (15m)

Notes for the kernel team (technical)
- Pay attention to loop interchange around the Q*K inner loop (we swapped two loops in last patch). The change increases stride on the inner product for common dims (seq<=128).
- Try alternate tiling that keeps contiguous loads for matrix B; hypothesis: reduces L2 misses.
- Microbenchmark suggestion: run a matrix multiply with shapes (128,64)x(64,128) with and without prefetch. See attached command in /tools/bench/kernels.sh

Mini experiment results (afternoon)
- Baseline (stable branch) small_model_v2, seq=64, batch=8: p50=28ms, p95=44ms
- After kernel-rewrite (current dev): p50=45ms, p95=72ms
- After revert microkernel locally: p50=31ms, p95=48ms
- After cache-key normalizer + microkernel revert: p50=30ms, p95=46ms -> suggests both fixes are additive

Open questions / unknowns
- Why is the CUDA memgrowth only on node-a-07? Could be firmware or driver mismatch; check nvidia-smi -q and driver versions across pool.
- Are there traffics patterns (client SDK) that attach metadata headers by default? Should sanitize at SDK level too.

Random TODOs / housekeeping
- Add a unit test for cache-key normalization (edge case: tool-call header order variance)
- File issue to CI to add nightly microkernel regression test (matrix shapes: 32/64/128 / batch 1..16)
- Remind infra to re-image node-a-07 if driver mismatch found

Useful links / refs
- PR 987: attention microkernel rewrite (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987)
- Linear RINF-2123 (latency regression) and RINF-2211 (kv-cache-normalize)
- Slack thread: #runtime-kernel (timestamped thread linked above)

Scratch wishlist (longer term)
- More automated kernel A/B testing on real traffic (sampled %) with canary routing (low-latency traffic only)
- Better observability: per-kernel timing in traces (span per operator)

Last quick note: capture all perf traces for the 2026-03-12 10:00-12:00 window and upload to /mnt/scratch/omar/perf/2026-03-12 for the postmortem.

End of scratchpad.
